answer: In an agent marketplace trading jade, orchard fruit, and saffron, dispute votes are weighted by tokens locked in escrow, with the same lock period for every identity. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up capital for the full lock period; generating more identities adds no influence.
